faq.q: Will this tell me what to buy?
faq.a: No. It is education about how crypto assets work and how to judge their risks. It is not investment, tax or legal advice.

faq.q: Do I need to own crypto?
faq.a: No. All labs run in your browser with made-up numbers.
No. They are teaching figures chosen to show a method, and the course says so wherever it matters.

activities.title: What does a round trip really cost?
activities.objective: Add up trading fees, the spread and a withdrawal fee to see what you keep.
activities.scenario: You buy 50,000 rupees of a crypto asset on an exchange, the price does not change, and you sell it again. The exchange charges a trading fee on each trade, a spread (you buy slightly above and sell slightly below the mid price) and a flat withdrawal fee. (Illustrative figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the buy fee: amount times the fee rate (B3).
In B8 work out the spread cost on the buy: amount times the half-spread (B4).
In B9 work out the value you hold after buying: amount minus the fee and the spread cost.
In B10 work out the sell fee on that value: value times the fee rate.
In B11 work out the spread cost when selling: value times the half-spread.
In B12 work out what you receive in the end: value minus sell fee, sell spread cost and the flat withdrawal fee (B5).
In B13 work out the total cost as a percentage of the amount you started with: (amount minus final) divided by amount.

checks.label: B7 is the buy fee
B8 is the buy spread cost
B9 is the value after buying
B10 is the sell fee
B11 is the sell spread cost
B12 is the final amount
checks.explain: Subtract sell costs and the flat fee.

checks.label: B13 is the total cost share

cells.A13: Total cost as a share of the amount

activities.title: Dollar-cost averaging versus a lump sum
activities.objective: Compare investing a fixed amount each month with investing everything at once.
activities.scenario: You have 6,000 rupees to invest. One plan invests 1,000 each month for six months; the other invests all 6,000 in month 1. Prices are made up. Work out units, average cost and final value.
steps: In C2 work out the units bought in month 1: 1,000 divided by the price. Fill down to C7.
In B9 total the units bought with the monthly plan using SUM.
In B10 work out the average price paid: total invested (6,000) divided by units.
In B11 work out the units from investing 6,000 at the month 1 price.
In B12 work out the value of the monthly plan at the last price: units times B7.
In B13 work out the value of the lump sum at the last price: B11 times B7.

activities.title: Read a token's vesting schedule
activities.objective: Work out how many tokens are unlocked over time and what that does to circulating supply.
activities.scenario: A token has a total supply of 1,000,000. The team gets 20% with a 12-month cliff (nothing unlocks before month 12) and then unlocks linearly over the next 24 months. The public sale gets 30% unlocked at launch. The rest (50%) is a treasury locked for 36 months. Work out the circulating supply at several months.
steps: In B2 to B6 the months are given (0, 12, 24, 36, 48).

In C2 work out the team's unlocked tokens: if the month is at or before the cliff (B8) nothing, otherwise the smaller of 1 and (month minus cliff) divided by the vesting period (B9), times the team allocation (B10). Fill down.
In D2 work out the treasury's unlocked tokens: if the month is below the lock period (B11) then 0 else the treasury allocation (B12). Fill down.
In E2 add the public sale tokens (B13), the team unlocked and the treasury unlocked. Fill down.
In F2 work out the share of the total supply that is circulating: E2 divided by the total (B14). Fill down.

checks.label: C2 is zero at launch
C4 is the team's unlock at month 24
checks.explain: Half the vesting period has passed.

checks.label: C6 is fully unlocked at month 48
D5 unlocks the treasury at month 36
checks.explain: At the lock period the treasury is released.

checks.label: E4 is the circulating supply at month 24
checks.explain: Public sale plus team plus treasury.

checks.label: F5 is the circulating share at month 36
